<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:main-local}
Let $K$ be the trefoil or figure-eight knot.  The fiberwise elliptic
involution defines a double branched cover
\[
 M_K\times S^1\longrightarrow T^2\times S^2.
\]
Its branch surface is the disjoint union $B_1\sqcup B_3$ of a section and a
connected three-fold multisection.  Both components are tori, and
\[
 [B_1]+[B_3]=4[T^2\times\{\mathrm{pt}\}]
 \quad\text{in }H_2(T^2\times S^2;\mathbb Z),
 \qquad B_1^2=B_3^2=0.
\]
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:main-obstruction}
The involutions induced on the boundaries of a fiber neighborhood and a
fixed-section neighborhood are not equivariantly diffeomorphic.  If a
fiber--section branch cobordism realizes these boundary covers, the two
boundary inclusions into its double cover cannot both be isomorphisms on
$H_1(-;\mathbb Z)$.  In the $X_5^{\rm sym}$ and $X_3$ constructions, the
natural local involutions do not preserve the chosen connected relative
smoothings with their prescribed boundary collars.  For the natural
$X_3$ elliptic involution, no connected invariant relative smoothing has
these collars.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:general-hyperelliptic-block}
Suppose that the capped monodromy of a genus-$g$ fibered knot $K$ is
hyperelliptic in the preceding sense, and choose $f$ with
$f\iota_g=\iota_gf$.  Then $\iota_g\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1}$ defines an involution
on $(\widehat\Sigma_g\times_fS^1)\times S^1$, identified with
$M_K\times S^1$, and its quotient map is a two-fold branched cover
\[
 M_K\times S^1\longrightarrow T^2\times S^2.
\]
The branch locus is a braided multisection of degree $2g+2$.  Its connected
components are tori indexed by the orbits of the induced permutation of the
$2g+2$ Weierstrass points.  If $A=[T^2\times\{\mathrm{pt}\}]$, then
\[
 [B_K]=(2g+2)A,\qquad B_K^2=0.
\]
In particular, the conclusion holds for every genus-one and every genus-two
fibered knot.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
For the chosen commuting representative $f$, the involution $\iota_g$
descends to the mapping torus and acts trivially on the additional circle.
The quotient of
$\widehat\Sigma_g$ by $\iota_g$ is $S^2$, branched at its $2g+2$
Weierstrass points.  Hence the quotient of $M_K\times S^1$ is
\[
 (S^2\times_{\bar f}S^1)\times S^1.
\]
The induced map $\bar f$ preserves the marked branch set and is
orientation preserving.  After forgetting the marked points it is isotopic
to the identity because $\operatorname{Diff}^+(S^2)$ is path connected
\cite{Smale}.  Choosing such an isotopy gives a noncanonical
fiber-preserving identification of the ambient quotient with
$T^2\times S^2$, while the motion of the marked points is retained as a
spherical braid.

Near a fixed point, the involution has the local form
$(z,u)\mapsto(-z,u)$, where $z$ is the oriented normal coordinate to the
fixed surface and $u$ is tangent to it.  Its quotient is smooth, and the image of the fixed
set is a smoothly embedded branch surface.

An orbit of length $r$ traces a connected $r$-fold cover of the first base
circle.  After taking the additional circle it gives a torus mapping
unbranched to $T^2$ with degree $r$.  Thus $B_K$ is an embedded oriented
union of tori, $e(B_K)=0$, and $[B_K]\cdot F=2g+2$.  Under the chosen
product identification write $[B_K]=(2g+2)A+dF$, where
$F=[\{\mathrm{pt}\}\times S^2]$.  With self-intersection computed in the
quotient orientation, note that $M_K\times S^1$ is a product with a closed
oriented three-manifold and therefore has signature zero.  Since
$\sigma(T^2\times S^2)=0$, the double-cover signature formula gives
\[
 0=2\cdot0-\frac12B_K^2.
\]
Here $B_K^2$ denotes the total normal Euler number of the possibly
disconnected branch surface.  Hence $B_K^2=0$.  As
$((2g+2)A+dF)^2=2(2g+2)d$, it follows that $d=0$.

For $g=1$, every mapping class has a linear representative commuting with
the elliptic involution induced by $-I$.  For $g=2$, the hyperelliptic
mapping class group is the full mapping class group.  Equivalently, every
mapping class is represented by a diffeomorphism commuting with a fixed
hyperelliptic involution; this is the genus-two realization statement in
the Birman--Hilden theorem \cite{BirmanHilden}.  This proves the last
assertion.  For $g\geq3$, hyperellipticity is not automatic; the hypothesis
is a sufficient condition for this fiberwise construction.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:surface-bundle-hyperelliptic}
Let $E\to T^2$ be an oriented $\Sigma_g$-bundle whose structure group
reduces to
\[
 C_{\operatorname{Diff}^+(\Sigma_g)}(\iota_g)
 =\{h\in\operatorname{Diff}^+(\Sigma_g):h\iota_g=\iota_gh\}
\]
for a fixed hyperelliptic involution $\iota_g$.  Then the fiberwise maps
$\iota_g$ define an involution on $E$.  Its quotient is an oriented
$S^2$-bundle over $T^2$, and $E$ is its double cover branched along a
braided multisection of total degree $2g+2$.  The branch components
correspond to the orbits of the induced monodromy action on the Weierstrass
points.  For $E=(\widehat\Sigma_g\times_fS^1)\times S^1$, with $f$ as in
Theorem~\ref{thm:general-hyperelliptic-block}, the quotient sphere bundle is
the product $T^2\times S^2$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
The reduction of structure group makes the local fiberwise involutions agree
under all transition maps.  Taking the quotient fiber by fiber gives the
asserted sphere bundle and branch multisection.  The quotient need not be the
trivial $S^2$-bundle in general.  In the product-mapping-torus case, one
clutching map is the identity and the other is isotopic to the identity in
$\operatorname{Diff}^+(S^2)$, so the quotient bundle is trivial.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:MKcover}
There is a double branched cover
\[
 \pi_K:M_K\times S^1\longrightarrow T^2\times S^2.
\]
Its branch locus $B_K$ is a degree-four braided multisection satisfying
\[
 [B_K]=4[T^2\times\{\mathrm{pt}\}],\qquad B_K^2=0.
\]
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
This is Theorem~\ref{thm:general-hyperelliptic-block} with $g=1$ and the
chosen product trivialization of the quotient sphere bundle.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:split}
For the standard trefoil and figure-eight monodromies,
\[
 B_K=B_1\sqcup B_3,
\]
where $B_1$ is a section and $B_3$ is a connected three-fold multisection. Both
components are tori.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
The four fixed points of the elliptic involution are identified with
\[
 T^2[2]\cong(\mathbb Z/2)^2.
\]
The monodromy acts linearly on this set. For the standard trefoil and
figure-eight genus-one monodromies, its reduction modulo two has order three.
It fixes the origin and cyclically permutes the three nonzero vectors. The
orbit decomposition is therefore $1+3$.

The corresponding components of the branch locus are respectively a section
and a connected three-fold cover of $T^2$. Every finite unbranched cover of a
torus is again a torus.  Write $[B_1]=A+d_1F$ and
$[B_3]=3A+d_3F$.  Since the components are disjoint,
$B_1\cdot B_3=3d_1+d_3=0$, while $d_1+d_3=0$ follows from
$[B_K]=4A$.  Hence $d_1=d_3=0$; in particular
$[B_1]=A$, $[B_3]=3A$, and both components have square zero.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
The branch locus is a degree-four multisection, but in these examples it is
not connected. The $1+3$ decomposition is useful because the section component
provides a geometric marker in the quotient picture.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def:marked-block}
A \emph{marked local branched-cover model} consists of a two-fold quotient
$p:\widetilde V\to V$ of connected manifolds, its branch surface $B$, the
covering character $\chi_p:\pi_1(V\setminus B)\to\mathbb Z/2$, and the
peripheral markings used below.  A marked summing surface in $\widetilde V$
is a square-zero surface, not necessarily invariant, with an ordered
symplectic basis, a positive meridian, and basepoint paths in its complement.
When $V$ is a surface bundle and $B$ is a braided multisection, we call this
a \emph{braided local model}.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\label{rem:globalization-criterion}
For the specified local involutions and markings, the local actions extend
to the closed manifold only if every gluing map is isotopic, through marked
boundary maps, to an equivariant map and the
induced quotient maps identify
the branch pairs and their restricted covering characters.  A braid word
does not determine the normal-circle class.  For a construction involving
smoothings or blowups, the chosen smoothing and blowup data must also be
equivariant, with compatible local framings.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:eqsum}
Let $(X_i,\iota_i)$, $i=1,2$, be smooth double branched covers, and suppose
$C_i\subset X_i$ are closed oriented invariant square-zero surfaces meeting
$\operatorname{Fix}(\iota_i)$ transversely.  Choose invariant product
neighborhoods $\nu C_i\cong C_i\times D^2$ in which
$\iota_i(z,w)=(\iota_i|_{C_i}(z),w)$.  Suppose the fiber-sum gluing
\[
 \Phi:\partial\nu C_1\longrightarrow\partial\nu C_2
\]
intertwines these product actions, reverses the oriented normal-circle
coordinate, and matches
the fixed boundary circles, their local intersection signs, the chosen
normal framings of $C_i$, and the local framings of the fixed surfaces at
$C_i\cap\operatorname{Fix}(\iota_i)$.  Then the fiber sum carries a natural involution and its
quotient is obtained by gluing the two quotient complements along the induced
boundary quotient map.  Equivariance also identifies the restricted covering
characters on the two quotient boundaries.  Near each transverse
intersection of a fixed surface with $C_i$, the branch surfaces are joined by
a local band attachment.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
The equivariant tubular-neighborhood theorem gives the stated invariant
product models, and equivariant isotopy extension allows the marked boundary
identification to be realized on collars.  The equivariant boundary
identification then makes the two actions agree on the union, and taking the
quotient commutes with gluing.  At a transverse
intersection choose oriented complex coordinates with the summing surface
$C_i=\{w=0\}$, the fixed surface $\{z=0\}$, and involution
$(z,w)\mapsto(-z,w)$.  The quotient map is $(z,w)\mapsto(z^2,w)$; matching
these models and the chosen local framings of the fixed surfaces gives a
smooth quotient.  On
$|w_1|=|w_2|=\varepsilon$, the standard collar gluing may be written
$w_2=\varepsilon^2/w_1$.  Thus the fixed annuli glue smoothly, and in the
quotient coordinates $u_i=z_i^2$ the branch loci $u_i=0$ join by the asserted
an annulus joining the corresponding boundary circles of the branch surfaces.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:boundary-obstruction}
The natural elliptic involutions on a fiber neighborhood and a fixed-section
neighborhood cannot be identified by an equivariant boundary
diffeomorphism.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
The fixed set of the fiber-boundary action is four circles, whereas the
section-boundary action is free.  Thus the actions cannot be equivariantly
diffeomorphic.  The same conclusion follows on first homology, since the
fiber-boundary action has eigenvalues $(-1,-1,1)$ while the section-boundary
action is the identity.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
A \emph{fiber-section branch cobordism} is a triple $(C,\mathcal A,q)$,
where $C$ is a compact oriented four-manifold from $S^2\times S^1$ to
$T^2\times S^1$, $\mathcal A\subset C$ is a properly embedded surface
transverse to the boundary and product near the boundary, and
\[
 \mathcal A\cap\partial_-C=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^{4}S_i^1,
 \qquad
 \mathcal A\cap\partial_+C=\varnothing.
\]
$q:\widetilde C\to C$ is a specified smooth double cover branched along
$\mathcal A$.  Fix boundary parameterizations by the displayed products.
The cover is required to have
boundary $T^3\sqcup T^3$ and to restrict, relative to these markings, to the
elliptic fiber cover on the incoming boundary and the free section-boundary
cover on the outgoing boundary.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:homology-product-obstruction}
Let $(C,\mathcal A,q)$ be a fiber-section branch cobordism, with deck
transformation $\tau$.  The two boundary inclusions $T^3\to\widetilde C$
cannot both induce isomorphisms on $H_1(-;\mathbb Z)$.  In particular,
$\widetilde C$ is neither an integral homology product nor a product
cobordism $T^3\times[0,1]$ relative to its boundary.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Suppose that the two boundary inclusions $j_-$ and $j_+$ induce isomorphisms
on $H_1$.  Equivariance gives
\[
 (j_\pm)_*\tau_{\pm *}=\tau_*(j_\pm)_*.
\]
The isomorphism
$\Phi=(j_+)_*^{-1}(j_-)_*$ then satisfies
$\Phi\tau_{-*}=\tau_{+*}\Phi$, so the two boundary actions are conjugate.  At the
fiber end, in the basis $(\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\mu_F)$, the action is
\[
 \tau_{-*}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,-1,1).
\]
At the fixed-section end, the deck transformation is a half-translation in
the normal circle and acts trivially on $H_1(T^3)$, so
\[
 \tau_{+*}=I_3.
\]
These matrices are not conjugate over $\mathbb Z$; their traces are $-1$ and
$3$.  This is a contradiction.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:no-collar-replacement}
There is no fiber-section branch cobordism whose specified double cover is a
collar $T^3\times[0,1]$ relative to the prescribed boundary markings.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
Both boundary inclusions of a collar $T^3\times[0,1]$ are homotopy
equivalences, contradicting
Theorem~\ref{thm:homology-product-obstruction}.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:x5-abp}
Each of the two summands in the twisted-double construction of
$X_5^{\rm sym}$ admits a local branched-cover model, but the natural
elliptic involution does not preserve the connected smoothing defining
$\Gamma_K$.  Consequently, the natural local involutions do not assemble
through this marked twisted-double construction.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
The twisted-double decomposition is \cite[Section~3.3]{ABP}; the ambient
cover follows by equivariantly blowing up a free orbit in
Proposition~\ref{prop:MKcover}.  The local formula above proves the
smoothing obstruction.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:x5-decorated}
The construction of $X_5$ is a fiber sum of three summands carrying local
branched-cover models.  Two are copies of
\[
 (M_K\times S^1,\iota_K)\longrightarrow
 (T^2\times S^2,B_1\sqcup B_3),
\]
where $B_1$ is a section, $B_3$ is a connected three-fold multisection, and the
nontrivial spherical braid monodromy is represented by
$\beta_{\rm tr}=h_\beta h_\alpha$.  The third is the Matsumoto
double cover
\[
 (Z,\tau_Z)\longrightarrow (W,B),\qquad
 W=(S^2\times T^2)\#4\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^2.
\]
Here $\tau_Z$ is the deck involution of $p:Z\to W$.
The marked fiber-section gluing $\phi_1$ defines $Y_K$, and the marked
genus-two gluing $\phi_2$ defines $X_5$.
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
The first two quotient pairs follow from
Proposition~\ref{prop:MKcover} and the splitting of the branch surface in
Proposition~\ref{prop:split}.  Section~\ref{sec:matsumoto} supplies the third
marked pair, including its horizontal and vertical branch components.  The
boundary identifications displayed below are the two gluing maps in the
covering manifolds.  No equivariance of these gluing maps is asserted.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:QK-cover}
For either genus-one fibered knot considered here, $Q_K$ is a two-fold
branched cover of
\[
 (T^2\times S^2)\#\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^2.
\]
The branch surface is the proper transform of $B_1\sqcup B_3$, disjoint from
the exceptional divisor.
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
Choose an orbit of two points in $M_K\times S^1$, disjoint from the fixed
set and exchanged freely by the natural elliptic involution, and blow up
both points equivariantly.  The involution
lifts and exchanges the two exceptional spheres.  Downstairs this operation
is one ordinary blowup at the image point.  Since the orbit was chosen away
from the fixed set, the branch surface is unchanged except for its proper
transform.  The covering manifold is
$(M_K\times S^1)\#2\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^2=Q_K$.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:k3-pi1}
The manifold $X_3$ is simply connected.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
After translating the generator conventions, the pushout is precisely the
group computed in \cite[Section~5, Lemma~13, and Appendix]{AP2008}.  The
relations established there include
\[
\begin{aligned}
 bhb&=hb^2h,& [d,hbh^{-1}]&=1,& [h,bdb^{-1}]&=1,\\
 d^2&=b^{-1}dbdb^{-1},& b^2&=hbh^{-1}bh,&
 h^2&=dhd^{-1}hd.
\end{aligned}
\]
The first three relations give $db=bd$; the fourth then gives $b=1$, and
the last two give $h=d=1$.  The marked gluing relations give
$a=g=y=z=1$, while $dbd^{-1}=x^{-1}$ gives $x=1$.  Thus
$\pi_1(X_3)=1$.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:k3-local-obstruction}
Let $B\subset\mathbb C^2$ be a sufficiently small $\tau$-invariant ball.
There is no connected $\tau$-invariant smooth surface in $B$ which is a
relative smoothing of $S\cup F$ and which agrees near its two boundary
circles with the prescribed section and fiber collars.
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
Suppose that such a connected surface $A$ with boundary exists.  Its collar on the section side lies
in $S=\{w=0\}$ and is fixed pointwise by $\tau$.  Average a Riemannian metric
on $A$ over the order-two action.  Then $\tau|_A$ is an isometry of the
connected surface $A$ which is the identity on a nonempty open collar.  An
isometry equal to the identity on an open set is globally the identity.
Hence
\[
 A\subset\operatorname{Fix}(\tau)=\{w=0\}.
\]
This is impossible because the other boundary collar agrees with
$F=\{z=0\}$ away from the origin, where the action is not pointwise fixed.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:no-swap-extension}
For the right-handed trefoil, no self-diffeomorphism of $M_K\times S^1$
carries the fiber torus $F$ to the section torus $S$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Let $A_{\rm tr}$ be the monodromy on the torus fiber.  The Wang sequence gives
\[
 H_1(M_K;\mathbb Z)\cong
 \mathbb Z\oplus\operatorname{coker}(A_{\rm tr}-I).
\]
Since $\det(A_{\rm tr}-I)=\pm1$, the cokernel vanishes and
$H_1(M_K\times S^1;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^2$.  The map induced by the
fiber inclusion factors through this cokernel and is therefore zero.  By
contrast, the mapping-torus circle and the external product circle generate
the section torus and map isomorphically onto $H_1(M_K\times S^1)$.
Thus the fiber inclusion has rank-zero image on first homology, whereas the
section inclusion has rank-two image.  A self-diffeomorphism preserves this
rank, so it cannot carry $F$ to $S$.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:x3-decorated}
The construction of $X_3$ admits three local branched-cover models.  Each
of its three copies of $M_K\times S^1$ carries the two-fold
quotient with branch surface $B_1\sqcup B_3$ and trefoil monodromy
$\beta_{\rm tr}$.  These are the marked pieces used in the construction of
$X_3$.  They yield a simply connected, symplectically
minimal, irreducible symplectic
manifold homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic to
$\mathbb{CP}^2\#3\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^2$.  The three natural local deck involutions do not extend
through the prescribed smoothing and gluing maps, so this statement makes no claim
that $X_3$ is a global double branched cover.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
The topology follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:k3-pi1} and the calculations above.
The failure to assemble follows from
Proposition~\ref{prop:k3-local-obstruction} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:boundary-obstruction}.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- question-1: body_md -->
\label{question:global-cover}
Does any of $X_5$, $X_5^{\rm sym}$, or $X_3$ occur as a double cover of a
four-manifold diffeomorphic to a rational or ruled surface, branched over a
smoothly embedded surface?
<!-- end question-1 -->
